Free -Day Shipping Get it by when you order within Get it if you order in Price: × Faster Shipping The Hizumitas was designed for the one and only guitar sorceress, Wata, from the legendary band, Boris! We could not be more excited to have the honor of working with such an iconic legend known for her crushing riffs and mind-melting leads. The Hizumitas is a faithful sonic recreation of her go-to distortion which has been a staple of her tone for many years: the Elk BM Sustainar. View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize Controls     1. Volume: Adjusts the output volume. Unity is around 9-10 o’clock. 2. Sustain: More distortion and sustain clockwise; less counterclockwise. 3. Tone: Boost bass frequencies clockwise and boost highs counterclockwise. This control has a massive effect on the character of the Hizumitas. Design Notes The Elk Sustainar is a Japanese variant of the more well-known “Triangle” BMP. During development, we used several vintage models of the BMP, as well as a few different versions of the Elk, and quickly realized all of them were wildly different. The only way we were going to truly capture the magic was to get our hands on her original pedal. Wata was kind enough to send her beloved pedal halfway across the world so we could see what made it tick. Right away, we realized it had something special that none of the others had - heavy saturation with a gritty edge and a massive bottom while still maintaining a clear and dynamic tone with enough mids and top end to cut through the sludge. We set out to faithfully recreate all these characteristics in the Hizumitas! The Hizumitas has loads of heavy distortion and smooth sustain with an underlying grit to it that sounds like the speakers are on the verge of ripping apart, all while still delivering amazing clarity that you wouldn’t expect from something this aggressive sounding. The Sustain control has a wide range of saturation, even small changes will have a great effect on the overall tone. The Hizumitas has excellent response to different pickup types and playing dynamics. Power chords sound huge and heavy, open chords are dynamic with fantastic note separation, and single-note leads are smooth and powerful, especially when using the neck pickup. The Tone control is atypical for this type of distortion and can drastically change the distortion’s character in conjunction with the Sustain setting. Bass frequencies are boosted clockwise while treble frequencies are boosted when turned counterclockwise. The treble side can go from piercing highs to an aggressive mid-range grind. As the Tone is turned clockwise, the mids become less present, highs are tamed, and a massive, thundering low-end comes to the forefront. As you might expect, there is plenty of output gain on tap, so be careful. Unity is around 9-10 o’clock and everything above that is set to destroy. Audio Samples Songs by Boris. Guitar by Wata. Hizumitas is a faithful recreation of Wata's go-to distortion pedal, the Elk BM Sustainar. The Elk is a Japanese variant of the very well-known Triangle BMP. The designers at EQD tried several vintage BMP's during development, found that each pedal was wildly different and realized that to truly capture the magic they needed the original. Wata graciously sent her beloved pedal halfway around the world, and EQD discovered that it had something special the others didn't have: heavy saturation with a gritty edge and massive bottom while maintaining a clear and dynamic tone with enough mids and top end to cut through any sludge. The studious wizards at EQD have built all of those characteristics into the Hizumitas! The pedal brings loads of heavy distortion and smooth sustain and an underlying grit that sounds like the speakers are on the verge of ripping apart while delivering amazing and unexpected clarity from such an aggressive sounding pedal. The Sustain control has a wide range of saturation, meaning even small changes will significantly affect the overall tone. Hizumitas responds excellently to all types of pickups and playing dynamics. Your power chords will sound huge and heavy, while open chords will be dynamic with fantastic note separation, and single note leads will come across smooth and powerful, especially with the neck pickup. The Tone control is atypical for this type of distortion and can drastically change the distortion's character in conjunction with the Sustain setting. Bass frequencies are boosted clockwise, and treble frequencies are boosted counterclockwise. The tone control can go from an aggressive mid-range grind to piercing highs as you turn it counterclockwise. As you turn it clockwise, the mids become less present, the highs are tamed, and a humongous, thundering low end comes to the forefront. The Volume control offers massive output gain with unity at around 9-10 o'clock and beyond that, prepare to hear and feel the power of Hizumitas! sources.excerpt: EarthQuaker Hizumitas: The Fuzz Wata Mailed To Akron Skip to content Dirty Guitar Facts. Loud Legends. R ock G uitars S tories P eople F orever Search GuitarGangsters ⌕ Menu Home Guitar Legends Gear & Rigs Guitars Amps Pedals & FX Pickups Accessories DIY Builds Custom Builds Electronics & Wiring Finishing & Relics Mods & Upgrades Rock History 70’s Rock 80’s Metal 90’s Grunge & Alternative 2000’s Revival News & Culture Videos About Contact In this guide What The Hizumitas Actually Is The Elk BM Sustainar: The Ghost In The Circuit Specifications The Controls, And The Knob That Works Backwards Famous Players Eight Settings Worth Stealing How It Compares Buying Guide Ownership Notes Frequently Asked Questions In this guide What The Hizumitas Actually Is The Elk BM Sustainar: The Ghost In The Circuit Specifications The Controls, And The Knob That Works Backwards Famous Players Eight Settings Worth Stealing How It Compares Buying Guide Ownership Notes Frequently Asked Questions Share this article Home › Gear & Rigs › EarthQuaker Devices Hizumitas: The Fuzz That Flew Halfway Around The World Gear & Rigs EarthQuaker Devices Hizumitas: The Fuzz That Flew Halfway Around The World EarthQuaker Devices Hizumitas guide: the Elk BM Sustainar origin, why the Tone knob is backwards, verified Wata and Jonny Greenwood use, plus 8 settings. admin 22 September 2026 19 min read Updated 26 September 2026 GG-ARTICLE-TOP There is a moment in every clone project where the engineers have to admit they are guessing. EarthQuaker Devices hit theirs early. They had gathered vintage Big Muff Pis. They had gathered several different Elk Sustainars. They plugged them in one after another, and what they found was chaos — every single unit sounded like a different pedal. Fifty-year-old carbon resistors and unmatched transistors had drifted so far apart that there was no such thing as “the” Elk sound to copy. GG-ARTICLE-AFTER-INTRO So they asked Wata to mail them her pedal. Her actual pedal. The one that has been the core of Boris’s guitar tone for the better part of three decades, the one that had already been broken and repaired more times than she wanted to count. She put it in a box in Japan and sent it to a workshop in Akron, Ohio. That is how the Hizumitas exists. Not as a tribute, not as a “in the spirit of,” but as a measurement of one specific, beaten-up, irreplaceable object — and then a production run of thousands built to match it. The result was announced on 4 November 2021, arrived with a purpose-recorded Boris track called Reincarnation Rose , and did something signature pedals almost never do: it retired the original. Wata took the Elk off her touring board and put the Hizumitas there instead. This is a feature, not a review. We are not scoring it. What follows is where the circuit came from, what a Japanese Big Muff bootleg from 1973 actually sounds like, why the Tone knob works backwards, which players are genuinely documented using this thing and which attributions we could not stand behind, eight settings worth stealing, and an honest read on who should buy something else. What The Hizumitas Actually Is Strip away the story and you have a three-knob, four-transistor-topology fuzz in a standard EarthQuaker enclosure: Volume, Sustain, Tone. It is a Big Muff Pi derivative in the broad sense — the Elk was an unlicensed Japanese copy of the “Triangle” era circuit — but it is not a Big Muff clone in the way a modern reissue is. It is a clone of a clone that had drifted, and the drift is the point. EarthQuaker’s own copy is unusually specific about what they were chasing: “heavy saturation with a gritty edge and a massive bottom while still maintaining a clear and dynamic tone with enough mids and top end to cut through the sludge.” Every clause in that sentence is doing work.
